Wang Bi’s base text here (執古之道，以御今之有。能知古始，是謂道紀) matches Legge’s key verse. The paraphrase holds: the formless and nameless as ancestor of all things; though times shift and customs change, none fails to rely on it to achieve order (‘every age’ is a fair gloss of 雖今古不同 … 莫不由乎此); antiquity remote but its Tao remains, so the ancient beginning can be known now. Linking ‘that Tao’ to the formless ancestor follows his own 故可執古之道 in the same comment.
